answer: Sybil resistance comes from quadratic staking: each agent locks a bond, and voting weight grows only with the square root of that bond. A raider who splits capital across a thousand fake cedar keys gains no extra influence, yet must post and risk a full bond on each, so attack cost rises linearly with identities while power stays flat. A public random beacon picks auditors who verify that one bonded key signs once per epoch; double-signing slashes the whole saffron bond. That single stake becomes the agent's anchor, making a swarm of cheap pseudonyms strictly worse than one honest identity.
